title.narrative: Training of Youth Peer Educators on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights in Mozambique (PET in SRHR)

description.narrative:
The proposed project must contribute to the following ++objective++:
- Universal access to sexual and reproductive health and rights (SDG 3 and 5).
The proposed project must contribute to at least one of the following ++long-term impacts++:
- More respect for the sexual and reproductive rights of groups who are currently denied these rights; - Better public and private health care for family planning, pregnancies and childbirth, including safe abortions; and/or - Better information and greater freedom of choice for young people about their sexuality.
The following ++medium-term impact++ will contribute to this:
- Partnerships between persons and organisations are inclusive and sustainable (SDG 17); - Organisations key to (sectoral) inclusive development of partner countries are strengthened by inflow of enhanced workforce.
This will be achieved by the following ++outcome++:
- Enhanced knowledge and skills of individuals and organisations (in partner countries and in the NL) in line with country/regional specific labour market needs and aiming at inclusiveness.
++Outputs++:
- Staff of CDD and 45 youth leaders improved their Knowledge and training skills in SRHR. - CDD youth leadership training module on SRHR developed, tested and ready for use in training young girls and boys during summer school. - A network of youth leaders in SRHR formed and used CDD platform to engage young girls an boys on SRHR issues. - 45 youth peer education trainers organized leadership change making interventions or outreach services.
​

actual.value:
**1. Training needs assessment of participants conducted**
The project conducted a Training Needs Assessment (TNA) to ensure the development of a gender and age sensitive curriculum. This assessment helped module development and careful design of the course to address the youth SRHR challenges and gaps and to support innovative and contextually sensitive peer education training strategies.
**2. Training modules are designed**
The project developed a nine-module curriculum with a focus on: gender and sexuality, social norms, maternal and reproductive health, sexual and gender based violence, youth livelihoods, leadership and peer advocacy. The project also conducted quality checks and these modules were translated into Portuguese.
**3. 45 peer educators trained on SRHR **
The project exceeded the original milestone of 45 and trained a total of 81 youth peer educators within March to June 2021. These peer educators came from three districts in Mozambique (Gaza, Manica and Xai-Xai-Gaza) representing diverse sectors, including: health centers and clinics; government service providers from justice law and order sector (JLOS) including police academy, prisons and judicial service; CSO workers and NGOs, CBOs that work with vulnerable youth (including HIV infected youth, male and female street youth, sex workers, drug addicts, refugees and internally displaced people, sexual minorities); and educational institutions including TVET.
The training helped participants improve their capacity to provide their peers with SRHR information and influence their decision-making. The training also built the confidence of young peer leaders working in clinical and non-clinical SRHR service spaces to design and implement peer education programmes in SRHR thus strengthening a multisectoral response to addressing SRHR challenges.
**4. Leadership change projects implemented and SRHR leadership networks established **
CDD supported 73 peer educators in designing and implementing change projects to strengthen SRHR interventions in their organizations, institutions and community. The project provided participants with modest funding and technical support to ensure effective implementation of their change projects within their communities. The participants designed and implemented various change projects, including educational campaigns, radio/tv programmes, community bazaar programmes, youth sexuality and family life campaigns, plays at school, and informal conversations with young people at clubs/parties.
The project also successfully established an SRHR leadership/advocacy platform as the peer educators cascaded the curriculum through their personal and professional networks. Over 8 months after implementation, the project had reached 3,146 young people (1,732 females and 1,414 males) with significant SRHR messages, including relevant information on Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STDs) and prevention methods. 11 health facilities are also collaborating with and supporting 18 of the peer educators in their outreach activities, including in distributing condoms to 2,500 beneficiaries. The project will also engage these health facilities on adopting youth-friendly approaches for delivery of SRHR services. With the support of Centro para Democracia e Desenvolvimento (CDD), the 81 youth peer educators will continue cascading knowledge and extending SRHR services through their networks.

title.narrative: CDD staff and strainers organised youth summer school on SRHR to cascade the training to 105 young girls and boys yearly.

comment.narrative:
- CDD staff and trainers organized youth summer school on SRHR to cascade the training to 105young girls and boys yearly.
- 100% of the participants in the summer school complete the training

11-04-2023: Instead of a youth summer school on SRHR, a "Transformational Leadership Academy" (TLA) was organized by CDD to cascade information not only on SRHR but also more broadly on leadership, communication, and advocacy skills. The TLA draws on the gender and age-sensitive modules and transformative teaching methods employed by the YPET in SRHR project. The first cohort of 30 youth leaders (15 females, 15 males) graduated from TLA in November 2022 in the city of Pemba. These young people were selected from the provinces of Nampula, Niassa, and Cabo Delgado.
